conviction_note: FY26 is the third print in a row where the only quantified revenue number is at risk (9M organic +0.2% against a ~2% full-year guide implies +5.6-7.4% in Q4) and the day also carries first-time FY27 guidance into a 24x FY27 multiple; the bear case largely agrees with a disclosed short that ran 0.70%->1.83% in six weeks, so it is substantially priced, and I am held to -2.0 rather than the -3.4%/-9.9% this name printed on its last two FULL results because the issuer is buying ~40% of daily volume and the short trimmed to 1.63% on 17/09. print_vs_bar (-1.0) is smaller than expected_move (-2.0) because the reported quarter is well telegraphed and the move is a guidance-and-reaction-function event, not a reported-number event.

The FCA historic aggregate series gives the whole dated path: 0.90% (02/07), 0.70% (31/07), 0.81% (06/08), 1.00% (13/08), 1.40% (20/08), 1.61% (25/08), 1.41% (28/08), 1.61% (07/09), 1.53% (11/09), 1.73% (15/09), 1.83% (16/09, became historical 17/09) -> 1.63% now. findings.finding: Smiths' own FY26 guidance of '~2%' organic revenue growth, set on 21 May 2026, requires Q4 (May-July 2026) organic growth of roughly +5.6% to +7.4% against nine-month organic of +0.2% and a flat Q3 - i.e. an exit rate at the top of the company's 5-7% medium-term ambition, in one quarter, from a standing start. Citi has since said the Middle East drag that cost Q3 GBP10m persists into FY27, which makes the required snap-back harder rather than easier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time this line disappointed - HY26 on 20 Mar 2026, where H1 continuing organic was only +0.4% and the outlook was cut to 3-4% - the shares fell 9.87% over this stage's own window (2350p -> 2118p). By contrast the 21 May 2026 Q3 cut of the FY organic guide itself cost only +0.32%, so a forward-looking trim is tolerated on this name while a delivered miss in a full results statement is not.
findings.why_not_priced: It is arithmetic off a public RNS, but it is not in any preview I could find: the Barclays reinstatement (18 Sep) and the Jefferies PT cut (21 Sep) both argue the multi-year case (FY27 ~3% organic, EPS falling to 105.3p) and neither tests whether the FY26 number the company itself quantified is reachable. If the market had priced a FY26 organic miss the stock would not have firmed +2.39% over the five sessions into the print while the 20-day run-up is -1.31%. The honest discount: with 14 analysts on the name this is the class of item that IS usually in a preview, which is why it is sized at a point rather than three.
findings.independence: Citi (Martin Wilkie, Buy) cut FY27 underlying forecasts ~2% specifically because 'disruption linked to the Middle East continues into the next financial year' and expects the John Crane recovery delayed - a different house and a different document: https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1095948/smiths-forecasts-trimmed-as-john-crane-recovery-slows-1095948.html

findings.finding: The scale of a Smiths FULL results print is 3-10%, not the ~1% the baseline carries, and both of the last two were negative. Using Investegate's dated RNS record and Yahoo daily closes: FY25 preliminary results 23 Sep 2025, 2378p -> 2298p = -3.36%; HY26 20 Mar 2026, 2350p -> 2118p = -9.87%. The two light trading statements in between moved -0.98% (Q1, 19 Nov 2025) and +0.32% (Q3, 21 May 2026). The sealed baseline's history omits the FY25 preliminary results entirely and substitutes the 9 Oct 2025 'Annual Financial Report' filing (+0.41%), which is the annual report publication and not a results event - so its median_abs_move of 0.69% and event_move_proxy of 1.09% understate this specific print type by a factor of 3 to 10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This IS the reaction history. The load-bearing observation is that HY26's -9.87% happened on the SAME day Smiths announced a further GBP1.5bn of shareholder returns, so on this name good capital-return news has not offset a disappointing growth outlook in a full results statement. FY25 prelims (-3.36%) likewise came with FY26 guidance of 3-4% that has since been cut twice.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no European single-stock option chain, so there is no event-implied move and nothing in the price states a scale out loud. What is observable is that the baseline this stage ranks on - and any reader who takes its history at face value - is carrying 1.09% for an event whose two most recent comparables were -3.4% and -9.9%. If the market were positioned for a 5-10% event the disclosed short would not have trimmed 0.20pp in the three sessions before it and the 5-day run-up would not be positive.
findings.independence: The -9.87% is corroborated independently of the tape: Investing.com reported the shares down 5.96% intraday at 2210p on 20 Mar 2026 (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/smiths-group-hy2026-slides-33bn-portfolio-shift-shares-fall-6-93CH-4572495), consistent with a 2350p base and a 2118p close. Shares one document with finding 1 only in that both use the 20 Mar 2026 event; the claims are different objects (fundamental risk vs reaction scale) and their sizes are not additive evidence for the same fact.

findings.finding: The issuer is absorbing roughly 40% of its own daily traded volume and must keep doing so through the print: the second buyback tranche was upsized from GBP400m to GBP700m on 28 July 2026 and 'is expected to complete no later than 31 December 2026', with only ~GBP84m done at 27 July, and the weekly Transactions in Own Shares RNSs run 1.64m-1.97m shares a week (~380k/day) against a median daily turnover of $31.2m (~900k shares). A further GBP1.5bn on-market programme follows through CY2027. The disclosed short of 1.63% (~5.95m shares) is therefore ~6.6 days of total ADV, or ~16 days of the company's own buying, in a float the company is shrinking by ~15% a year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Untested on this name in the current configuration - the buyback only reached this run-rate after the 23 July 2026 General Meeting granted 14.99% authority, so no results print has yet occurred with a bid this size underneath it. The two dated positioning-relevant RNS days since did move the stock up: Detection completion 30 Jun +1.23%, pension buy-in 21 Jul +2.42%.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline scores this crudely: short_squeeze +1.098 against short_building -2.0, net negative, using a stale 1.83% and no knowledge at all of the size of the offsetting issuer bid. If the asymmetry were priced, the short would not have been pressed from 0.70% to 1.83% in six weeks into a programme that is buying ~40% of the volume those shorts have to cover into. This is a positive-tail finding and it deliberately does not contradict findings 1 and 2 - it widens the band and lifts the mean, it does not reverse the central case.
findings.independence: The short side is from a different publisher: FCA aggregated net short positions workbook, Current ANSP 1.63% at 2026-09-16 and the full dated historic path, https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-net-short-positions.xlsx . Share count from BlackRock's TR-1 of 7 Sep 2026 (37,734,095 = 10.33%), https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/smiths-group--smin/holding-s-in-company/9759687

findings.finding: GBP1.66bn of pension de-risking completed INSIDE FY26 (year ended 31 July 2026) and only GBP760m of it was ever announced: the TI Group Pension Scheme's GBP900m full BUYOUT completed in May 2026 with no standalone RNS - it surfaces only as a subordinate clause in the 21 July SIPS announcement - and c.15,500 members are now insured by Aviva, L&G, PIC and Rothesay. The CFO's stated effect is cash, not cosmetics: 'removes pension risk and future cash funding requirements and reduces balance sheet volatility. This improved financial flexibility strengthens free cash flow'. FY26 results are the first document that quantifies it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one observable datum is the 21 July 2026 announcement of the smaller (GBP760m) half, which moved the shares +2.42% (2564p -> 2626p) - a large reaction for a transaction the RNS says required no company contribution, which suggests the market values the legacy-liability removal more than its cash cost. Nothing was paid for the GBP900m buyout because nothing was announced.
findings.why_not_priced: Half of it was never disclosed as a regulated announcement, so no preview could have modelled it: I checked SMIN's full RNS list for May 2026 on Investegate and there is no pension announcement between the 1 May Total Voting Rights and the 26 May Transactions in Own Shares. Sized small and with a band through zero on purpose: the direction is genuinely two-sided, because derecognising two insured schemes will also put a large non-cash IAS 19 settlement/remeasurement through the FY26 statutory accounts, and I could not verify either the schemes' IAS 19 surplus or any employer top-up in a primary document. It is filed as one_off, not guidance, because the company has not yet put a number on the free-cash-flow path.
findings.independence: Independently reported by the insurer and by the pensions trade press: M&G's own release (https://group.mandg.com/news-and-insights/press-releases/2026/21-07-2026) and Pensions Age, 21 Jul 2026 (https://www.pensionsage.com/pa/Smiths-Industries-Pension-Scheme-completes-760m-buy-in-with-M-G.php), both of which also carry the GBP900m TI buyout as a May 2026 event.

lessons_applied: 'Coverage tells you which regime you are in' - analyst_band is >13 (14 analysts), so the Q4 arithmetic in finding 1 is the class of item a preview usually carries. Cut it from -1.3 to -1.0.

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error' plus 'the tail is intact, so do not size as if it were not' - raised finding 2 from -1.2 to -1.8 and widened its band from roughly [-4.0,+1.0] to [-6.0,+1.5], because this name's own full-results distribution is -3.4% and -9.9% and there is no price limit to truncate it.

'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with... a crowded short is fuel' - raised finding 3 from +0.8 to +1.1 and widened its high to +4.0; also the reason the negative findings are sized well below the name's realised full-results moves, since they largely restate the building short.

'Two findings that cannot both be true are resolved by you, now' - checked findings 1/2 (negative central) against finding 3 (positive tail) and wrote the reconciliation into finding 3: it is a band-widener, not a sign flip. Findings 1 and 2 share the 20 Mar 2026 event but make different claims; said so in independence.
'Keep findings inside the exit window' - moved the GBP1.5bn CY2027 programme, the 31 Dec 2026 tranche deadline and the November AGM authority renewal out of findings into outside_window at zero.

Impact sum moved from -1.4 to -1.4 (unchanged in total: -0.3 on finding 1, -0.6 on finding 2, +0.3 on finding 3), and expected_move_pct was held at -2.0 rather than pulled toward the sum, because baseline_tension reads agree-with-lean rather than cut-against, so the file's shrink rule does not bite.
